doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Charlotte's family and the three Georges
summary: Charlotte's son lives in California; they sort out George I, II and III, a grandson in the reserve band holding his grandfather's last cornet.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: I have a son, but he didn't pick up any music. He lives in California, my baby.

She's six years and seven months older than him. I don't know if you say stuff. She's six years and seven months older than him. He was just four years old when his daddy died. Ernest. Bring the father back to daddy.
I knew George, what did he go? S. George III?
Who? S. George, yeah, because daddy was the first. George's daddy, my husband's daddy, was the first man. And his son was the second. And his son was the third.
He was in awe with him.

He was in reserve. I think, but they don't have no more reserve band. He's still in reserve. He's just as fat as a hog. He was on a Friday evening. Just so fat. But his mother wouldn't have been able to keep up the music. He's got two saxophone, a cornet. He got his daddy's last cornet. He got two cornets. Yeah, you know that cornet that, with the bell along? Well, the last one got a trumpet, my dad, long. Well, Judge Judy's got that.
